title: Complete Existence Classification of Seven-Partite Absolutely Maximally Entangled States
authors: Fei Shi, Xiande Zhang, Qi Zhao, Lvzhou Li
abstract: We prove that an absolutely maximally entangled state of seven qudits exists if and only if the local dimension satisfies $d\geq 3$. Prior to this work, to the best of our knowledge, $\text{AME}(7,d)$ states were known to exist only when $d$ is a prime power other than $2$, or when $d$ can be expressed as a product of dimensions for which existence was already known. Since it has been proved that no $\text{AME}(7,2)$ state exists, it remains to establish existence for all $d\geq 3$. We construct cyclic quadratic-phase states for every odd local dimension and develop a coupled binary--odd-dimensional construction for every dimension congruent to $2$ modulo $4$. Together with the known power-of-two cases and the product property of AME states, these constructions cover every local dimension $d\geq 3$.
summary: The paper achieves the complete existence classification for absolutely maximally entangled (AME) states involving seven qudits. It proves that such states exist for all local dimensions $d \ge 3$. The proof combines novel constructions for various dimensional forms with rigorous mathematical analysis of state marginals.
main_problem: The primary goal is to establish a complete existence classification for absolutely maximally entangled states (AME) involving seven qudits, denoted $	ext{AME}(7, d)$.
main_result: The authors prove that an AME state of seven qudits exists if and only if the local dimension $d$ satisfies $d \ge 3$.
method: The proof involves constructing specific quantum states (cyclic quadratic-phase states for odd $d$, coupled binary–odd-dimensional constructions for $d \equiv 2 \pmod 4$) and analyzing the vanishing of cross-terms in the three-party marginals using character orthogonality.
model_or_system: The system under study is a multi-partite quantum state involving seven qudits, whose entanglement properties are characterized by the existence of AME states. These states are mathematically linked to pure quantum MDS codes with parameters $[[7, 0, \lfloor 7/2 floor + 1]]_d$.
key_observables: The three-party marginal $ho_S$ is a key observable; its proof of proportionality to the identity operator ($\mathbb{I}/D$) confirms the AME property.
important_parameters: The local dimension $d$ is the critical parameter, with existence proven for all $d \ge 3$.
main_assumptions: The classification relies on known results regarding non-existence at $d=2$ and utilizes a product property: if two states are AME, their tensor product is also AME.
figures_summary: Table I lists simplex codes and coset representatives; Fig. 1 illustrates the Fano plane structure on $\mathbb{Z}_7$; Table II provides certificates showing vanishing cross-terms in specific products involving shift vectors.
paper_structure: The paper first addresses the general problem of AME existence, then details constructions for odd dimensions ($d=q$) and dimensions congruent to $2 \pmod 4$ ($d=2^k q'$). The structure builds upon known cases (prime power dimensions) to cover all remaining $d \ge 3$ using product rules.
why_interesting: This work provides a definitive classification result for a specific, highly structured class of multi-partite entangled states, which has deep connections to quantum error correction codes and the fundamental limits of entanglement in multipartite systems.
